newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 10.

text.p: Five people were left isolated on the road near a rampaging Raurimu gunman for two hours on Saturday till the armed defenders squad could reach them. Six people died in the central North Island massacre, and another six were injured, one critically. Page 1.

The Queen has sent her sympathies to the families of those shot at Raurimu. In a message to Governor-General Sir Michael Hardie Boys, she said she was appalled to hear of the tragic loss of six lives and knew all New Zealanders would share the

A showdown is looming between NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan and Tainui leader Sir Robert Mahuta. Morgan is furious about a statement by the Tainui Maori Trust Board that alleged he "sought excessive consultancy fees of $250,000" for his part in establishing a proposed Tainui Television station. Morgan believes Mahuta is responsible for the statement. Page 2.

Aotearoa Television staff had no indication whether the Cabinet would make a decision today on the Maori station's future or what that decision would be, spokeswoman Gillian de Beer said on Sunday. The television station ran out of money on Thursday and has been surviving on staff goodwill and a backlog of programmes. Page 2.

Opposition politicians are questioning the ability of health and disability commissioner Robyn Stent to conduct an inquiry into patient safety at Christchurch Hospital. Health Minister Bill English dropped plans for a ministerial inquiry into the
hospital on Friday after Stent announced her own inquiry. Page 2.

The government should cut its new spending proposals by $100 million, Manufacturers Federation chief executive Simon Arnold said on Sunday. Industry would be looking for signs of government determination to improve its management of the economy in Tuesday's presentation to business leaders by Treasurer Winston Peters, Arnold said. Page 2.

Defence Minister Paul East favours buying more Anzac frigates as Australian pressure intensifies for a favourable decision later this year, according to a report on Sunday. After a softly-softly approach by Australia last year because of New Zealand elections, Prime Minister John Howard was expected to apply renewed pressure on Prime Minister Jim Bolger when he visited New Zealand for three days from Saturday, the Sunday Star-Times said. Page 2.

Progressive Enterprises can expect to report a substantial lift in earnings for the first half to January 31 and a better performance in the 1997-98 financial year, chief executive Graeme Kelly said. He also said that the supermarket chain had remedied its breach of interest rate covenants with its banks and had reduced debt by about $70 million to $80 million from a peak of $210 million a year ago. Page 17.

World wool supplies could rise by about three percent to 1.68 million tonnes during 1996-97, according to the International Wool Textile Organisation. But despite improved trade clearances by the main wool producers and increased sales from growers' holdings, "the wool market remains fundamentally oversupplied", the IWTO says in a published report. Page 17.
